newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: De Beers edges closer to Russian deal.
newsitem.headline: De Beers edges closer to Russian deal.

text.p: Diamond giant De Beers said on Tuesday that it is edging closer to a deal with Russia on a new marketing agreement.

Russia missed a New Years Eve deadline on signing a new deal and the temporary arrangement that had held sway until then ceased to exist. De Beers' London-based Central Selling Organisation (CSO) controls some 75 percent of the rough diamond market.
CSO managing director Gary Ralfe told a news conference that the process of discussions had gone well during a trip to Russia three weeks ago.
"The process seems to be moving ahead satisfactorily following the suspension of the old agreement," he said.

Ralfe said he hoped soon to have a resolution signed by Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin authorising the signing of a new agreement and a decree from President Boris Yeltsin that will make a modified memorandum of understanding signed in February 1996 a constitutional agreement.
"Things are moving ahead and we hope within the next couple of months to have those two final authorisations," he said.
Ralfe said it is important to bring the Russian federal government into the agreement in order to ensure a repeat of the deal breakdown did not occur. "That is something we would welcome," he said.
Ralfe declined to say what the modification to the memorandum of understanding would be. "The details of our agreement will remain confidential," he said.
However, Ralfe added that -- in another step towards ensuring there are no further breakdowns -- a new deal could be a roll-over contract.
"The contract would not be an evergreen contract. It would be something that we could roll on quite easily," he said,
